# The result of a fold of two limbs: the state, or NaN

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `fold_finish_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The result of a fold from its final state $s$: the state itself when its leading limb is finite, with the flag $\mathit{flag}$ true; otherwise a NaN in every limb and the flag false (the canonical NaN of [When something is not finite](../developer/design/milestone2.md#sum-dot-axpy-convolution)):

$$r = s \ \text{when } s_0 \text{ is finite}, \qquad r = \mathrm{NaN} \text{ otherwise}.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $s = s_0 + s_1$, $r = r_0 + r_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `A.sum()` | `Accumulator<T, 2>` | `Reduction<Expansion<T, 2>>` | the running sum of an accumulator, canonical; the finish of the loops of `kairn/batch.hpp` too |

`T` is `float` or `double`; `A` and `B` are accumulators, `kairn::Accumulator<T, k>`, header `kairn/accumulator.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` includes. They take no marker: an operation of an accumulator compiles only while its kernels are proved ([The accumulator](accumulator.md)).

## Requires

- every limb of $s$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $\mathit{flag}$ is true exactly when $s_0$ is finite.
- When it is, $r = s$, limb for limb.
- Otherwise every limb of $r$ is a NaN.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `fold_finish_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeFoldFinish.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeFoldFinish.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions fold_finish_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `fold_finish_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the finish of a fold: the state or the canonical NaN (milestone2.md). **License:** proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/fold_finish_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/fold_finish_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The finish of a fold of two limbs (milestone2.md, "When something is not finite"): the final
# state when its leading limb is finite, with the flag true; otherwise the canonical NaN, (NaN,
# NaN), and the flag false. A finite leading limb of the final state means that every state before
# it was finite (the non-finite cone of the steps): the bridge of Milestone 1 applies step by step.

a    = abs(s0)
flag = lt(a, const inf)
r0   = select(flag, s0, const nan)
r1   = select(flag, s1, const nan)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#fold_finish_2)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 102 600 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 102 600 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 6 domains of 6 formats | 2 861 220 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
